newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares shake off worries to climb higher.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares shake off worries to climb higher.

text.p: Milan shares shook off concerns over continued warnings that southern European nations will struggle to meet the conditions for entry to a single European currency and ended higher on Thursday.

The dollar firmed after Russian President Boris Yeltsin sacked his security chief Alexander Lebed and this helped the lira recovery ground lost earlier in the day. But many other stock markets were lower after tame U.S. economic data did little to lessen concern over U.S. earnings.
The all-share Mibtel index ended up 0.6 percent at 9,885 while the Mib30 blue chip eased 0.75 percent to 14,919.

On the U.S. data, the Philadelphia Fed index showed an economy continuing to soften in October while August business inventories were up more than expected. Dealers said the effect was largely neutral amid concern over U.S. earnings growth.
Stocks largely ignored further warnings on Italy not meeting EMU criteria, while dealers watched for any developments from the Prodi-Kohl meeting today in Bonn.

Among individual stocks, Montedison edged above the 1,000 lire level as analysts pointed to its anti-cyclical strengths and how it would gain from a fall in interest rates. The stock closed up 1.67 percent at 1,016 lire.
Fiat continued its recovery up 1.93 percent to 4,058 lire after hitting fresh lows earlier this week on concern over the continually weak Italian car market.
Olivetti held firmer up 1.21 percent at 477.4 lire even after Mediaset denied press reports that it was interested in taking over the troubled information technology group.
